title: Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time (B1 open, not a witness)
body:
# Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time, which spends the whole complex branch

**κ = 416977294469409/500000000000000000 = 8.339545889388e-4**, and `binding = complex` for the
first time on this ladder: **+14.5981% over #246's rung** (`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` =
7.277211262868e-4). The schedule those absorptions need is **measured here, not merely owed**: the
retained bit row is re-derived, every family's two readings of the bank criterion are applied, the
leader's three absorptions are applied by hand -- a whole family out, the padding per bank drawn
out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the bank count -- and the point is priced
through the unchanged 47-constraint assembly. The claim is still a **priced target on a scheduled
row**: conditional on C1-C7 and on #219's inherited R1-R4, whose PRs are unmerged and pinned by
digest. Not a witness.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run3/`, self-contained on the branch, extended in place. It vendors
#219's rung-1 package byte-identically under `references/pr219-run1/` and #207's frontier
certificate and #233's row, and pins **66 files by sha256**.

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3 && python3 -B verify.py
```

## Result

The ladder has been **bit-bound since rung 2**, and the leaf that bounded it had been treated as a
constant of #219's word. It is not one: the rung-1 retained row is a ledger with thirteen more
bankable families in it, and every absorption lowers the retained mass, so the leaf itself moves.
The rank-3 rung on #233's row (`bitrung.py`'s baseline, and #246's point):

| rung on #233's row (head `109a857`, pinned by digest) | value |
| --- | --- |
| banks | 4,086 (1,362 per copy), 22 rank-3 blocks × 3 registers, **padding 0** |
| retained coarse saving | `417325324839139/5·10^17` = 8.346506496783e-4, the next 10⁻¹⁸ grid point up excluded |
| budget | the bit leaf `7.282510899902e-4` — **bit-bound**, so the complex supplier did not bind |
| **κ** | **`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4**, `binding = bit` |

The screen: thirteen of the retained row's 21 families can leave into whole width-72 banks or into
the padded schedule a bank admits, so every rung of up to three of them is priced (13 + 78 + 286 =
**377 rungs**), by the vendored interval-moment engine. The leading rows, exactly as `bitrung.json`
records them (the gains are the recorded kappas divided by the rank-3 rung's):

| absorb | banks | retained W | bit leaf | kappa | binding | gain over #246 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| rank 20 | 5,280 of 3 blocks + 12 registers | 45,006 | 7.957727174054441e-4 | `397569983356707/500000000000000000` = 7.95139966713414e-4 | bit | +9.2644% |
| ranks 4, 20 | 6,878 (rank 4 exactly filled, rank 20 as above) | 43,408 | 8.337650404202950e-4 | `104133806924797/125000000000000000` = 8.33070455398376e-4 | bit | +14.4766% |
| rank 21 alone | 15,018 of 3 blocks + 9 registers | 35,268 | 9.319873169802724e-4 | `416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4 | **complex** | +14.5981% |
| **ranks 7, 8, 20 (the leader)** | **7,342** (1,224 of 10 blocks + 2 registers; 838 of 9, exact; 5,280 of 3 + 12) | **42,944** | **8.349765438523530e-4** | **`416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4** | **complex** | **+14.5981%** |

| against | value | gain | asserted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the rung below, on the same row (#246) | `1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4 | **+14.5981%** | asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| the frontier this package prices against (#207) | `1366380910073/2·10¹⁵` = 6.831904550365e-4 | +22.07% | the comparison is asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| this package's previous top (the padded rung 4) | `711599961413937/10^18` = 7.11599961413937e-4 | +17.19% | stated |
| the record published on `main` (#186) | `330942774629799/5·10¹⁷` = 6.61885549259598e-4 | +26.0% | stated, dated |
| the highest other open claim at the time of writing (#257) | 7.104652045e-4 | +17.4% | stated, dated |

The two *asserted* rows cannot drift: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives both numbers from the
pinned bytes and asserts the comparisons (there, the two gains are exact quotients of recorded
values). The three *stated* rows are dated observations of this package and of the queue, and are
labelled as such.

## Why the bit leaf was the lever, and what the criterion is

#219's rung 1 absorbs the rank-22 family of the PR200/PR205 packed bit word into 6,116 whole
width-72 banks and leaves a retained row of `W = 50,286` roles, rank mass 3,614,784, deficit 5,808
and 857,622 children over 21 ranks, whose certified paid saving -- bootstrapped through #185's
three-level chain -- is the leaf `7.282510899902e-4`. Every reading of this package so far priced
*that* row as it stands, which is why the earlier sections concluded that `7.5e-4`, `8e-4` and
`1e-3` were out of reach on this word. `bitrung.py` prices the row one rung further: a second family
can leave the **same** retained ledger into whole banks, the way the rank-22 bin did, and the leaf
rises by **+14.6550%** to `8.349765438523530e-4`.

The criterion is rung 1's, restated on the retained row and read two ways, because the two readings
are not the same rung:

* the **volume** reading: the family's own volume is a whole number of width-72 banks,
  `72 | rank * n_rank`;
* the **padded** reading: what a bank can actually host when the rank does not divide the width --
  `capacity = 72 // rank` blocks of the family plus `72 mod rank` registers of padding in every
  bank, so it needs saturation (`capacity | n_rank`) and a retained bin that can supply the padding.
  This is T1's padded schedule, one word over, and the module checks rather than asserts that each
  padded step needs its own bank count: rank 7's volume reading prices 1,190 banks where its
  schedule needs 1,224 (`1,190 × 10 = 11,900 < 12,240` items), and rank 20's prices 4,400 where its
  schedule needs 5,280 (`4,400 × 3 = 13,200 < 15,840` items).  The rung prices the schedule, not the
  accounting.

The schedule keeps the retained row's identity: `W = 42,944`, rank mass 3,086,160, deficit 5,808,
756,192 children over 18 families, the stock dropping by exactly the 7,342 banks, and **65,808
registers of padding in all** drawn as a partial removal from the singleton bin -- exactly what T1
does on the complex side.

**The binding side changes here, and that is the result.** The leader's leaf sits *above* the
complex branch it has to clear (the rung reaches `1.000390455784346` of that branch), so the budget
is the branch `417325324839138999999999582174675160861/5·10⁴¹` and the kappa is
`416977294469409/500000000000000000`, the last `10⁻¹⁸` grid point at or below #233's row's complex
ceiling `417325324839139/500417325324839139`. So the wall moves rather than disappears: every
further bit rung is capped by the complex side, and the next increment is the complex supplier
again -- or a new bit word that lifts the leaf without spending the branch.

## The plateau: 108 rungs, one point

**108 of the 377 screened rungs** price `416977294469409/500000000000000000`, because once a rung's
bit leaf clears the complex branch the budget is the branch and every such rung lands on the same
point: the screen is not choosing among them, the cap is. The point therefore does not depend on
which rung is quoted; only the cheapest bank count does, and the package's own leader rule (highest
kappa, ties broken by the fewest banks, then by the sorted ranks) is why the claimed rung is ranks
7, 8 and 20 at 7,342 banks rather than rank 21 alone (15,018 banks) or ranks 4 and 21 (16,616).
Both sides of the plateau are asserted: every rung that carries the point is complex-bound, and
every bit-bound rung lands strictly below it.

## What proves it

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3
python3 -B verify.py            # check: pins, rebuild, compare with certificate.json, bitrung.json and occurrences-bitrung.json
python3 -B bitrung.py           # the measurement: writes bitrung.json
python3 -B bitinstance.py       # B1: the item maps, bank tables, padding draw and induced ledger
python3 -B importer66.py --self-test   # the harness's own thirteen cases
cd references/pr219-run1 && python3 -B verify.py   # the vendored rung-1 package, in place
```

`verify.py` pins **66 files by sha256** -- the 37 this package owns (bitrung.py, bitinstance.py and
their two artifacts among them, and the ranked heads of #233), the two upstream certificates it is
priced against (#207's frontier and #233's row), the 16 the vendored rung-1 package of #219 carries
and the 11 of the bit drop -- and
rebuilds the whole complex-side ladder (base, rung 2, rungs 3 and 4, both paid moments per rung,
the two 47-constraint assemblies with adjacent-grid rejection, the eligibility and width scans, the
PR208 replica, the padded schedule, the instanced inventories and all three export contracts), then
checks the new rung: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives the rung-1 retained row **from the
pinned packed certificate with plain integer and `Fraction` arithmetic, no package module and no
engine**, re-checks every family's two readings, applies the leader's three absorptions by hand
(whole family out, the padding per bank out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the
bank count), re-runs the bootstrap chain and the assembly rule, computes the kappa on the grid
below the bound, asserts the leader's minimality on the plateau and both comparisons above, and
compares the whole measurement with `bitrung.json`. `verify.py -> check_bit_instancing` does the
same for B1: it rebuilds the instancing, recomputes both digests from the addressing rule rather
than trusting them, re-checks the padding as a partial removal from the singleton bin, asserts that
the induced ledger is the row `check_bit_rung` prices, and asserts that the pins still export no
block and no occurrence of these three families. verify.py reproduces #207's, #219's and #224's
published grid points, and the rank-3 rung's own, exactly -- the bit rung's complex branch *is* the
rank-3 rung's recorded coarse saving, which `check_bit_rung` asserts rather than assumes.

The package's own path-filtered workflow (`.github/workflows/complex-bank-ladder.yml`, 3.11, 3.13,
3.14: `verify.py`, the vendored package's self-check, the three contracts' self-tests, then
`git diff --exit-code`) and the repository test module (`tests/test_complex_bank_run3.py`, which now
also asserts this rung's kappa, its complex binding, the leader and the plateau) cover it. The
change extends the package's own files (`bitrung.py`, `bitrung.json`, `verify.py`, `pins.py`,
`run3.py`, `obligations.json`, `README.md`, the regenerated `SOURCE.json` and `certificate.json`) and
the test module; the pinned vendored inputs, the other rungs' artifacts and the three export
contracts are untouched.

## Status

* **B1 is `INVENTORY_INSTANCED_AT_SCHEDULE_LEVEL`** (`obligations.json`), the bit side's second
  absorption: its schedule half is **instanced** -- `bitinstance.py` gives every one of the 35,622
  items of ranks 7, 8 and 20 a bank, a block and an offset, fills every bank exactly with the
  family's blocks plus the padding it draws, names the 65,808 registers of that padding item by
  item out of the retained singleton bin (digested, `1828/10481` of the bin), digests each family's
  bank table, and re-derives the ledger the absorptions induce (stock 50,286 -> 42,944, rank mass
  3,614,784 -> 3,086,160, 857,622 children -> 756,192 over 18 families) from the pinned packed
  certificate. Its **provenance half is open**, and machine-read rather than asserted: the pins
  carry no key containing `block` or `occurrence` for this word -- the packed certificate's single
  `assign` key is its own rejection control -- so each of those 35,622 items has an address and no
  identity, and the shape owed is #219's rank-22 inventory, key for key (`H`, `H_center`, `Y`,
  `src`). The no-other-bin-moves proof is owed with it.
* **R1-R4** (inherited verbatim from #219) and **C1-C7** are unchanged: the normalizer, the formal
  columns, the charts and prime witnesses, the envelope parity and each child's frame/chain
  provenance. The absorbed families need the new residual types the suppliers' proofs reserve,
  exactly as the complex rungs do, and the rows are pinned by digest to unmerged branches.
* No witness, no completed finite witness, no unconditional multiplication theorem, no practical
  multiplier, and no Lean/kernel certificate is claimed -- here or anywhere in this ladder.

## Scope and limits

* The measurement is over the retained bit ledger of #219's rung-1 word at width 72, and over
  rungs of up to three families. Longer rungs are not screened; on this cap they cannot change the
  point, but that is not measured.
* The whole-bank volume condition is necessary and is what the built rungs use; it is not
  sufficient, which is exactly why the padded schedule exists and why the module records where the
  volume-criterion bank count fails to host its own items.
* A moved branch fails `check_manifest` closed and the measurement must be re-taken: the head of
  #233's row is pinned by digest.
* Nothing here bounds any other bit or complex lever: a different word, width or frame layout is
  not priced.

on** and is credited as such, and #233's source-assisted row and #246's rank-3 rung are what make
the complex branch the productive side at this point. Rung 2 and the ceiling argument are #224's,
the ladder and its replica convention are #208's, the bank proof and the engine chain are
#200/#205/#206/#197's (Chafik Boukhalfa and the #197/#205 line), #184/#168-v4's (icekylinx,
eumemic), #183's and #193's, and #185's bootstrap chain is what the bit leaf is read through;
nothing is re-implemented or restated as new. Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance.
